method.value: Curve-of-growth aperture photometry; line flux within 0.3 arcsec radius; continuum within 8.5 arcsec radius; Gaussian fit to image

evidence.quote: Most of the H30$\alpha$ flux from the unresolved central source falls within a radius of 0.3 arcsec, so we will use the measurements of the line flux from within that radius as the total flux.

evidence.quote: We therefore think the ALMA flux density, which is consistent with the SEST measurement, should be fairly reliable.

analysis_steps.goal: Convert H30alpha flux to Q and SFR

method.value: Scoville & Murchikova equation with alpha_B and emissivity interpolated from Storey & Hummer; then Starburst99-based Q-to-SFR conversion for Z=0.0056 with/without rotation

evidence.quote: We interpolated among the $\alpha_B$ and $\epsilon_\nu$ terms published by (cite: storey95) to calculate specific values
we use 11500 K for the electron temperature

assumptions.value: Nuclear starburst contains most photoionizing stars; Kroupa IMF; continuous star formation >10 Myr; log Q scales linearly with Z; Z≅0.0056

evidence.quote: we assume that the nuclear starburst detected in H30$\alpha$ data contains most of the photoionizing stars in the galaxy

validation.value: Interpolation accurate to within 5% based on 1994 Geneva tracks

analysis_steps.goal: Compute SFRs from infrared data and total infrared flux

evidence.quote: We therefore calculated the total infrared flux by first linearly interpolating between the logarithms of the monochromatic flux densities as a function of the logarithm of the wavelength and then integrating under the curve.

findings_qualitative.value: H30alpha emission originates mainly from a compact central source (~0.15 arcsec deconvolved) coincident with the 231.6 GHz continuum peak; no second H30alpha source detected

evidence.quote: No significant H30$\alpha$ emission is observed outside of the central peak.

findings_qualitative.value: Mid-infrared tracers give much higher SFR because dust is unusually hot; recommended against in low-metallicity galaxies

evidence.quote: we strongly recommend not using any star formation tracer based on mid-infrared data for low metallicity galaxies.

claims.hypothesis: Does H30alpha give a reliable SFR for NGC 5253 and how do other metrics compare?
claims.experiment: Derive Q and SFR from ALMA H30alpha and compare to IR, Halpha and radio SFRs
claims.result: SFR 0.087±0.013 Msun/yr; TIR SFR 0.107±0.008 within ~1.5-2 sigma
claims.finding: Total infrared SFR statistically equivalent to H30alpha

evidence.quote: the SFR calculated from the total infrared flux was statistically equivalent to the values from the H30$\alpha$ data.

claims.hypothesis: Mid-infrared SFR metrics are reliable in low-metallicity dwarfs
claims.experiment: Compare 22 micron and Halpha+22 micron SFRs with H30alpha
